ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 driver-cancellation (rider no-show) fee; no voucher issued. No account action.

rejected_claims.reason: The tap-to-cancel gap is 3 min 5 s, not under three minutes; 185 s > 180 s, and NS-1(iii) requires only 'more than 3 minutes' [F6][F4][NS-1]. The driver was also stationary 3 min 25 s at 38 m from the pickup [F3].
Even measured from the 'I'm Here' tap, the in-radius wait was 3 min 5 s, above the threshold; the 4 min 30 s platform-arrival figure merely confirms the longer wait [F6][F5][F2][NS-1].

The finding does not rest on the driver's chat or post-trip statement; it rests on the GPS/timeline records (stationary 3 min 25 s at 38 m, 185 s in-radius after the tap, 38 m closest approach) which the statements merely track [F1][F2][F3][F6][F10][F12][NS-1].

NS-2's refund branch requires that one of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) fail; all three hold on the system records — tap at 09:56:20, 40 m at the tap, 185 s in-radius after the tap — so the $6.61 fee stands [F6][F1][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The flag request rests on profile facts alone (two upheld no-show disputes in 90 d), which RD-6 permits only as an add-on and never as the basis of a finding; RD-6 is not reached here because there is no refund and no recorded RD-1 breach in this case [F17][RD-6].

Accepted as correct (NS-1(i) is met via the 09:56:20 tap), but it does not carry the case: the waiting element (iii) is also met, so the claim that the fee 'rests entirely' on a failed three-minute wait does not follow [F6][F3][NS-1].
